subject: gk
question: Which of the following provisions of the Constitution of India requires a special majority of the Parliament and the consent of the states?

options.text: Abolition and creation of Legislative Councils

solution:
The correct answer is __**Presidential Elections**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Presidential elections in India are governed by Article 54 and Article 55 of the Constitution.
 
• The election requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament and the legislatures of at least half of the States.
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college, which includes elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• A special majority means a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, plus the majority of the total membership of each House.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electoral College for Presidential Elections**

 
 
• The electoral college consists of elected members of both Houses of Parliament.
 
• It also includes elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• Nominated members of Rajya Sabha, Lok Sabha, and Legislative Assemblies do not participate in the election.
 
 
 
• **Voting System**
 
 
• The election follows a system of proportional representation using a single transferable vote.
 
• Each elector marks preferences for candidates in order of choice.
 
• The candidate who secures more than half of the total value of valid votes is declared elected.
 
 
 
• **Special Majority Requirement**
 
 
• A special majority refers to a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, plus the majority of the total membership of each House.
 
• This ensures wider consensus and legitimacy for the highest constitutional office.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President**
 
 
• The President of India is the ceremonial head of state, supreme commander of the armed forces, and the signatory for all laws passed by Parliament.
 
• The President plays a crucial role in the legislative process and can summon or dissolve Parliament sessions.
